title: DCGS-A option-set, support, correction, and substitution denominator · first pass

sources.title: U.S. Army releases DCGS-A Increment 2 request for proposals
retrieved_facts: The Army described a fifteen-month user and vendor market-research process before the 2015 solicitation.
The Army represented the acquisition as full and open competition intended to maximize competition among commercial vendors.
The announcement does not supply the complete contacted-vendor, bidder, evaluated-architecture, support, or later performance denominator.

sources.title: Palantir USG, Inc., B-412746
retrieved_facts: Palantir challenged the single-integrator DCGS-A2 solicitation as insufficiently attentive to commercial-item acquisition.
GAO denied the protest, concluding on the record before it that the Army had conducted adequate market research and had a reasonable basis for the integrated single-contractor approach.
The decision records commercial, government, open-source, phased, and integrated-system alternatives rather than a Palantir-only universe.

sources.title: Palantir USG, Inc. v. United States, No. 17-1465
sources.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit
retrieved_facts: The Court of Federal Claims permanently enjoined the solicitation after concluding that the Army failed to comply with the commercial-item market-research requirements of 10 U.S.C. § 2377.
The Federal Circuit affirmed the injunction.

The judicial result demonstrates an external correction route and a legal defect in the challenged acquisition process; it does not by itself establish later foreclosure, favoritism, or Palantir superiority.

sources.title: General Dynamics Mission Systems, Inc., B-416181
retrieved_facts: A later Capability Drop 1 competition evaluated multiple offerors and product demonstrations.
The Army selected Raytheon and Palantir as ready for award and rejected the General Dynamics proposal as technically unacceptable under specified requirements.
GAO denied General Dynamics' evaluation protest after reviewing the disclosed record.
The decision confirms an alternative and protest denominator but not complete equality of data, support, testing opportunity, or later performance.

chronology.event: Army issues DCGS-A Increment 2 solicitation after claimed market research and full-and-open-competition planning.
GAO denies Palantir's preaward challenge to the acquisition approach.
Court of Federal Claims enjoins the solicitation for noncompliance with commercial-item market-research requirements.
Army awards later Capability Drop 1 contracts to Raytheon and Palantir.
GAO denies General Dynamics' technical-evaluation protest.
Federal Circuit publicly issues its precedential opinion affirming the injunction in the earlier Palantir challenge.
